Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

aggressive adjective

also aggression, aggressively, combative, belligerent, quarrelsome, fierce

classical

Cic. Rep. 5.10: ācer et pugnāx (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 2.19.5: ōrātiō pugnāx et contentiōsa (Lewis & Short)

pugnāx, pugnācis

Declension on Wiktionary

aggressive, combative

Fond of fighting, of soldiers, peoples, cockerels and rams (Petr. 86; Col. 7.3.6); of a speech or a speaker, contentious; in an argument, obstinate (Cic. Pis. 70).

Other words

  • ferōx, ferōcis — fierce, wild, headstrong

    also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 43.4 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Vat. 4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Untamed and bold; in a good sense, spirited and brave (Plautus), but more often overbearing. Cicero gives it to youth: ferōcitās juvenum (Sen. 33).

Examples

  • nātūrā ferōx, vehemēns, manū prōmptus erat

    he was aggressive by nature, violent, quick with his fists (of Cethegus)Sall. Cat. 43.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • Cavē: canis ille ferōx est.

    Careful, that dog’s aggressive.composed

See also attack, violent, force.

SourcesLewis & Short: pugnax · Lewis & Short: ferox

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
